english.title: Assault enforcement officer / assistant exercising power under section 89 or 90
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) assaulted

(A)_[an enforcement officer, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OFFICER..),]_
(B)_[an assistant of an enforcement officer, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ASSISTANT..),]_

while

(C)_[he]_
(D)_[she]_

was exercising a power conferred by section 89 or 90 of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006
english.legislation: Contrary to section 92(1)(a) and 93(1) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
assaulted an enforcement officer/an assistant of an enforcement officer
while he/she was exercising a power conferred by s.89 or 90 of the Act

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 92(4) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 provides that a reference in sections 89 to 92 in relation to an enforcement officer's assistant, to the exercise of any of the powers mentioned in section 89(4) is a reference to the exercise by the assistant of any of those powers on behalf of the officer.
(ii) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.
(iii) The Wireless Telegraphy (Fixed Penalty) Regulations 2011, (In force 01/10/2011), introduces a £100-00p fixed penalty charge for summary only offences under the Act, as from that date. This regime does not include offences relating to illegal broadcasting (pirate radio).

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Twelve months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

Fixed Penalty charge of £100-00p (in force from 01/10/2011).

For offences committed before the commencement of section 282(3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003:
Six months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and/or fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
